title: Pathing Plus
description:
Every act starts the same way: you stare at the map, trace routes with your finger, and try to hold four of them in your head at once.

This mod does that part for you. Draw roughly where you want to go and it snaps your stroke to the nodes it passes, working out the real routes that fit, in the game's own hand-drawn style. Sketch through the elite you want and the fire you need after it, and see which ways through the act actually give you both.

Features include:

- Draw on the map and the mod fits paths to what you drew. The eraser rubs out steps you don't want; Clear Drawings starts over.
- Or click nodes instead: pin the ones you care about and the routes connecting them are worked out for you. Double-click a node to pin every node of that type at once (all the elites, all the fires).
- A replacement Legend that counts: node types down the side, one column per route. Hover a type to light up every node of that type on the map, hover a route to preview it, select it to lock it in. Hovering a drawn line on the map works the other way round and lights its column.
- Only finished routes are tabulated, so a plan you're halfway through drawing doesn't clutter the comparison. Draw to one step short of the end and the last step is drawn for you.
- Locked routes stay locked as you travel along them, and your plan survives closing the map - and closing the game.
- A Zoom button that cycles three views: the normal map, the whole act on one screen, and the whole act rotated on its side with the start at the left and the boss at the right.
- Full controller support. Right Trigger zooms, the left stick drives the quill, and the stick click swaps between quill and eraser - because drawing lines on a map with a gamepad isn't really a thing.

Informational only - the mod reads the map and draws over it. Nothing about the run changes, and a "?" node stays a "?".

Feedback and feature requests always welcome!

Source code and issue tracker:
https://github.com/davekalina/spire2-pathing-plus
changeNote:
v0.24.1

- Route highlighting is confined to the line between two nodes. It stays out of the way while you have the quill or eraser in hand, and no longer fires when you are pointing at a node you are about to click.

From v0.24.0:

- Hovering a route picks the line you are actually pointing at. It was testing against the nodes rather than where the lines are drawn, so every route in a bundle sat on the same spot and neighbours could not be told apart. The catch radius is much tighter now too.
- Routes with no column in the Legend can be hovered as well - they light up on the map even though there is nothing to highlight in the table.

From v0.23.1:

- A node you had erased can be clicked again. It was unselectable: the click pinned it, the erase still held it out of the plan, and it came straight back off - with nothing on screen to say why.
- Path markers lost their setting. They are small and they fade, which left nothing worth choosing between.

From v0.23.0:

- Draw to one step short of the end of the act and the last step is drawn for you.
- A pin the eraser has cut off from the rest of the plan is dropped rather than left as a ring with no path attached.
- Hovering a drawn route lights its column in the Legend, the mirror of hovering a column to light the route.
- Hovering a pinned node brings the markers back; they hold three seconds now rather than five.

From v0.22.0:

- The eraser takes off one node at a time. It used to lift the pin a whole leg hung from, so rubbing out a single step could take half the path with it. Erasing is also sticky now: a node you rub out stays out, and the route goes round it instead of straight back through it.
- The Legend always names the best five routes, however many match. A wide field used to fall back to an unlabelled tangle and an empty table, which said nothing about which way was better at exactly the moment you were asking.
- Path markers fade in when you change the plan, hold for five seconds, and fade out. A ring that stays put reads as "somewhere I have been", which is the wrong thing to see on a node ahead when you are choosing where to move - but it is useful feedback while drawing. Small is the default again.
- The controller's gold cursor ring no longer gets stranded on the map when you go back to the mouse.
